storiesChecked.verdict: contract conformant to every behavioural criterion; 1 ticked process criterion is not literally true; 1 story-level protection inactive by default

findings.specText: story-053 Accrual semantics: "maxPayout therefore caps the pot itself ... This is the accrual cap that prevents a long idle period from turning into one large mint." Contract shape: "uint256 public maxPayout; // ... 0 = unlimited". Concerns: "Pause does not freeze accrual." Out of Scope: "phStaging2: deploying NFTBonfire, ... setting the initial rate ... a follow-up story in phStaging2, ordered after phStaging2:116."
findings.actualBehavior: Code matches the letter of the story: maxPayout defaults to 0, pendingPayout() returns raw accrual when cap == 0 (line 120), and pause() does not stop accrual. So the story's own stated safeguard (the cap) does nothing until the owner sets it. The story hands the job of setting the initial rate to a follow-up deploy story but never lists setMaxPayout as part of that job, and that follow-up story does not exist yet (whole-tree glob for 'bonfire' finds only 053).
findings.deviation: Internal gap in the story, not in the code. The cap is described as the idle-period protection, but nothing in the story requires it to be set before the rate is enabled, and the default leaves it off. This is the same root cause as CODE-001 / ECON-001 (front-runnable retroactive cap, pause-then-unpause windfall). Filed here only so the spec-conformance report records that the follow-up deploy story must carry 'setMaxPayout before setRatePerDay, and pause -> setMaxPayout -> unpause for any later cap reduction'. Dedup against CODE-001/ECON-001 and keep their Low label.
findings.law1Assessment: No escalation. Total antimatter minted is never more than the integral of ratePerDay over time. setRatePerDay checkpoints before every change, so no time before the rate was enabled is ever paid out (the constructor-time lastUpdate is overwritten by the first setRatePerDay checkpoint). The cap only ever lowers emission. An uncapped default concentrates the intended dilution budget on one recipient; it does not increase that budget.

The executor disclosed this (Autonomous Decision 2) and the story was auto-completed with it carried forward as a non-blocking [medium]. No housekeeping story exists yet. Contract behaviour is unaffected.

story050LedgerAssessment.conclusion: Deleting the source is consistent with the wind-down. Nothing in the deployed instance keeps these findings live: it holds no value, has no outstanding approvals, receives no dispatches, and is paused. Its owner surface (withdrawBPT, rescueERC20, replaceDispatcher on the minter) is owner-only, and re-registering the pooler would be an obvious owner action (Law 3). Regression scans can no longer observe these entries because the source is gone, so they will otherwise sit 'open' forever. Proposal, for a human to apply via /ledger: close all 7 as wont-fix (obsolete: contract deleted in story-050, deployed instance unregistered, paused and drained; verified at block 26280480). They should not be closed as 'fixed', because no fix was made, and not as 'abandoned', because that status is for discarded branches and this code was merged. Never auto-flip.

law1StoryReview.story-053: No unsafe-story escalation. Front-running is knowingly accepted, and minPayout fully protects an honest burner (a reverted burn keeps the NFT). The uncapped default and the fact that pause does not stop accrual are knowingly accepted. Emission is bounded by ratePerDay x time, so these only concentrate the budget (see F-01-053, CODE-001, ECON-001). The 'all token IDs equal' rule means the cheapest NFT route sets the price (ECON-003, the V1+NFTMigrator route). That decides who captures the fixed emission, not how much is emitted. It is a footgun in on-chain wiring outside this story, and stays Low. The core caller-only invariant holds.
law1StoryReview.story-050: Source-only deletion; no on-chain effect. The deployed instance is verified inert.
